slides.headline: He is waiting for her to finish the glass.
slides.sub: Johannes Vermeer, The Glass of Wine, about 1658-60

slides.headline: A visit
slides.text: A young woman drinks wine, while a man stands over her holding the jug, ready to fill her glass again.

slides.headline: The glass
slides.text: She tips the glass up to her face, hiding it almost completely. We cannot read her expression at all.

slides.headline: The man
slides.text: He does not drink. He just waits, hand on the jug, his face shaded by the wide brim of his hat.

slides.headline: The window
slides.text: Now look at the stained glass in the open window. A woman holds reins: Temperance, the virtue of self-control.

slides.headline: The lute
slides.text: On the chair lies a lute, with sheets of music on the table. In Dutch paintings, music often hinted at love.

slides.headline: The landscape
slides.text: On the wall above them hangs a dark landscape in a heavy gilded frame, like a window onto a wilder world.

slides.headline: The floor
slides.text: Even the floor tiles lead our eye straight to the couple, as if the room itself were pushing them together.

slides.headline: Another glass?
slides.text: Another glass, or not? Vermeer freezes the moment before she decides. What would you tell her to do?
